content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of lean pork, carrots, broccoli and dark‑green leafy vegetables (spinach, kale, Swiss chard). It is prepared without potatoes or sauce, making it low‑calorie and nutrient‑dense.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pork is a rich source of high‑quality protein and vitamin B12.
Broccoli contains sulforaphane, a compound with antioxidant properties.
Carrots are high in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
Dark‑green leafy greens provide vitamin K, essential for blood clotting.
Omitting potatoes and sauce reduces simple carbohydrates and added fats.

items.title: Supports muscle mass
items.content: Pork protein aids growth and repair of muscle tissue.

items.title: Boosts immunity
items.content: B‑vitamins and zinc in pork help maintain immune function.

items.title: Eye health
items.content: Beta‑carotene from carrots is converted to vitamin A, vital for vision.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Sulforaphane from broccoli and polyphenols from leafy greens combat free radicals.

items.title: Bone support
items.content: Vitamin K and calcium from leafy greens contribute to bone mineralization.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Some cuts of pork can be high in saturated fat; choose lean portions.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Pork should be cooked to an internal temperature of at least 71 °C to eliminate salmonella and trichinella.

items.title: Meat protein allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may be allergic to pork proteins.

items.title: Interaction with medication
items.content: High vitamin K levels can affect the efficacy of anticoagulant drugs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, slicing the pork into thin strips and mixing with boiled or lightly sautéed vegetables. Optionally add a splash of lemon juice or fresh herbs for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 2 months. Reheat to at least 74 °C before consumption.
